overview:
Greg Stanton, the Democratic incumbent, enters the general election with a strong hand in Arizona's fourth district. The district leans Democratic by four points, and the fundamentals add a favorable national environment and a standard incumbency advantage. Stanton has raised $2.7 million and holds $1.9 million on hand, while Republican Zuhdi Jasser has about $90,000 in cash after raising $745,000. No outside groups are spending against Stanton, and prediction markets price his chances near 96 percent.

No public general-election polls are available, so the forecast rests on fundamentals and market pricing, and that absence of polling is the main source of uncertainty, reflected in a wide error band. Even so, every available signal points in the same direction, and a Libertarian candidate on the ballot is unlikely to change the outcome. The race is rated Safe Democratic.
